purpose: Empirical transport-only evidence for reusable Scheduled Runtime slots. This file does not promote relay v3 to production.
important_limitations: Slot transport probes after the initial generation use all-zero request digest/blob placeholders and therefore do not prove production immutable-request binding.
Scheduled Task metadata is non-canonical transport evidence until mechanically accepted and persisted.
Direct Scheduled Runtime GitHub writes remain unsupported/unreliable and were not used.
Observed fixed-slot self-metadata publication is still non-deterministic.

observations.note: Same physical Scheduled Task reused successfully for a later generation.

observations.title: ACP_READY|1|36d6108db3c5
observations.note: Independent second physical slot published successfully.
Runtime deliberately evaluated a false check and was instructed to stop without metadata publication, simulating lost publication.
Same-generation redelivery ran but self-metadata stayed unchanged. Therefore fixed-slot self-update is not deterministic and relay v3 must not yet be promoted.

current_conclusion: Reusable slots remove task-creation churn and have multiple successful publications, but self-update of the executing Scheduled Task remains a non-deterministic transport operation. Next diagnostic should separate producer execution from mailbox mutation by having a worker slot update a distinct disabled mailbox task.
